chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever enters Mecca as a Mutamatti' (one performing Umrah then Hajj) during the months of Hajj, he is not permitted to leave until he completes the Hajj. If a need arises for him to go to 'Usfan, or to Al-Ta'if, or to Dhat 'Irq, he exits in a state of Ihram and enters while reciting the Talbiyah for Hajj. He remains in his Ihram; if he returns to Mecca, he returns in Ihram and does not approach the House until he exits with the people to Mina in his Ihram, and if he wishes, his direction is towards Mina.

I asked: If he was unaware and exited to Medina or similar places without Ihram, then returned during the season of Hajj in the months of Hajj intending Hajj, does he enter in Ihram or without Ihram? He said: If he returns in its month, he enters without Ihram; and if he enters in a non-month, he enters in Ihram.
I asked: Which of the two Ihrams and two Umrahs is his Mut'ah, the first or the last? He said: The last one is his Umrah, and it is the one bound to which is connected his Hajj.

I asked: What is the difference between the Mufrid (one performing Hajj alone) and the Umrah of the Mutamatti' when he enters in the months of Hajj? He said: He enters with Ihram for Umrah while intending Umrah, then he releases from it, and there is no Dam (sacrifice) upon him, and he is not bound by it because he does not intend Hajj.

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and the first ten days of Muharram)
key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: Ihram (state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.الْمُفْرَدَةِ: Al-Mufradah (Hajj al-Mufrad, performing Hajj alone without Umrah)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Dam (sacrifice of an animal, usually a sheep, as expiation)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعاً: Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, combining them)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who leaves Mecca before completing Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the procedural nuances for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who temporarily exits Mecca during the Hajj months, emphasizing the continuity of their Hajj Ihram for short trips to nearby locations like Ta'if. It further clarifies the theological distinction between the Mufrid and Mutamatti' modes of Hajj, noting that the Mutamatti's Umrah is a distinct, released act without the binding obligation of a sacrifice (dam) since the primary intention was the subsequent Hajj. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view on the flexibility of ritual states during the sacred months.
